claims.text: Cr39Co18Fe18Ni18Al7 is initially in a high-temperature BCC state.
Locally heterogeneous lattice strains developed during cooling control the range of phases emerging in Cr39Co18Fe18Ni18Al7.
Thermal gradients and nonuniform cooling rates induce localized lattice strains.
Local thermal gradients can influence phase fractions and microstructural morphology in multiphase high-entropy alloys.
Localized strain fields alter local free energies and reduce the nucleation barrier for non-BCC phases.
Localized lattice strain and associated microstructural inhomogeneities act as nucleation sites for secondary phases.
Differential thermal contraction caused by temperature gradients produces localized lattice strain.
Regions of heightened strain can develop alternate FCC or HCP phases.
Strain-mediated formation of alternate phases produces a mixed-phase microstructure.
Uniform slow cooling with minimal thermal gradients maintains a predominantly BCC microstructure in Cr39Co18Fe18Ni18Al7.
Relative to uniform slow cooling, controlled thermal-gradient cooling will cause localized secondary-phase nucleation at sites of high lattice strain.
Secondary-phase fraction and spatial distribution will correlate with the magnitude and location of imposed temperature gradients.
Ultra-rapid quenching suppresses diffusion sufficiently to prevent the proposed strain-mediated phase formation.
The proposed mechanism should not operate when cooling or thermal exposure is sufficiently uniform or isothermal to eliminate significant thermal gradients and related strain fields.
The identity of the alternate phases may change with small compositional or environmental perturbations.
